name: correctness

findings.message: The DSCMBR-1 skip guard reads `stage_statuses[$s]` which is a flat, never-reset map: if the run is interrupted after `_cycle_state_write_iter_start` writes `current_iter=N` but before any member of iteration N has dispatched, every member still shows `complete` from iteration N-1, so the guard silently skips every member of iteration N — the entire iteration completes with zero dispatches and no stage.start events.

The read path sanitises `cycle_id` to `_safe_cycle_id` (stripping any character outside `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]`) before constructing the jq path, but the write paths (`_cycle_state_jq_write_iter_start`, `_cycle_state_jq_write_iter`) pass the original unsanitised `cycle_id` via `--arg id "$_ZB_CYCLE_ID"`; a cycle whose ID contains a stripped character (e.g. a dot) will be written under the original key but read under a different key, causing resume to silently return 0 for `_persisted_iter` and start from iteration 1 instead of the interrupted iteration.
